summary: Example two-play playbook updating Apache on webservers and PostgreSQL on databases with remote_user, and notes playbook keywords can control connection, privilege escalation and error handling at several levels.
questions: Can you show a simple playbook with multiple plays?
What does remote_user do in a play?
Where can I set playbook keywords?

answer_card.title: Example multi-play playbook
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- name: Update web servers
  hosts: webservers
  remote_user: root
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.yum:
        name: httpd
        state: latest
    - ansible.builtin.template:
        src: /srv/httpd.j2
        dest: /etc/httpd.conf

- name: Update db servers
  hosts: databases
  remote_user: root
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.yum:
        name: postgresql
        state: latest
    - ansible.builtin.service:
        name: postgresql
        state: started
```

`remote_user` is the SSH user. Other keywords (connection, become, error handling) can be set at playbook, play or task level, or via CLI, config and inventory.
